title: Information Diffusion in Financial Markets
subtitle: Event-time price adjustment around scheduled Federal Reserve communications
author: Joel Cerraga
status: research protocol, recorded before acquisition of study-period intraday responses
price_source: Dukascopy public historical ETF CFD quotes
price_definition: arithmetic average of BID and ASK minute closes; a midpoint proxy, not a synchronised consolidated-market midpoint
bar_label: UTC minute start; horizon h uses the close of the bar starting h-1 minutes after release
missing_data: No forward filling. Exclude an event-asset pair with a missing required minute, invalid OHLC, nonpositive prices, or a negative close spread. Preserve every exclusion.
control_days: First available date at 7, 14, 21 or 28 days before event, same local time and weekday, excluding all USMPD communication dates. Availability only, never outcome size, determines fallback.
surprise_transform: First covariance principal component of rate changes in basis points; centre and fit using scheduled development statements only; orient positive sum of loadings; divide by development score standard deviation. Transfer unchanged to validation, holdout and minutes.
surprise_timing: USMPD surprise incorporates the entire [-10,+20] minute window. Within-window regressions are retrospective associations, not implementable time-zero forecasts or identified causal speeds.
primary_regression: Cumulative log return in basis points at each horizon on intercept and standardised surprise; no contemporaneous equity-market subtraction.
primary_inference: HC3 pointwise intervals; event-level Rademacher wild-bootstrap simultaneous band across the 20 SPY statement horizons; separate two-sided 95% HC3 interval for the predeclared 5-to-20-minute slope.
adjustment_model: Signed amplitude A times [1-(1-f)exp(-k(h-1))], h>=1; f in [0,1], k in [0.01,5]. f is first-minute fraction, not a literal instantaneous tick jump. Fit to unrestricted estimated response curve.
speed_reporting_gate: Terminal 20-minute slope CI excludes zero; slope at 20 minus slope at 10 equivalent to zero within 25% of terminal magnitude using a 90% interval (heuristic estimated margin); monotone model normalised RMSE <=0.25; k and f away from numerical boundaries; at least 90% bootstrap fits valid. Report conditional model summaries only; otherwise mark speed unidentifiable.
robustness: baseline timestamp shifted -1 or +1 minute, labelled sensitivity
add pre-event return and volatility controls
matched-day return association with the paired event surprise
predictive lead-lag tests with own lags and event fixed effects
chronological_evaluation: Fit on development, inspect validation without selection from a parameter grid, retain the declared primary model. Before opening held-out intraday responses, hash analysis code and fitted development model. Compare holdout squared error with the development intercept-only prediction for cumulative 20-minute and 5-to-20-minute returns. These are retrospective transfer checks. A separate 20-to-25-minute prediction uses the surprise only after its observation window has closed.
extension: Apply frozen development-statement PCA to FOMC minutes releases; report event-type comparison as exploratory. No earnings-call claim without verified release/call timing and historical expectation data.
interpretation: One broker feed, one-minute resolution, a finite event sample and ex-post rate surprises cannot establish the exact time all information enters the underlying exchange price. A null or unstable lag result is retained. No trading-profit claim.
publication_stage: Executed notebooks and review artifacts only. Final paper typesetting and public GitHub release are separate subsequent stages.
